title: Improve VoiceOver reading order and token contrast ramp for dense tables with inline edit
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Users reported inconsistent VoiceOver traversal and incorrect reading order in dense table rows that include inline-edit controls and action menus. Separately, color token mappings for compact density and dark mode produce insufficient contrast at small text sizes (12–14px) in several table cells and badges. This ticket drives a combined design and accessibility remediation: fix screen-reader reading order, stabilize keyboard navigation in inline-edit flows, and revise token contrast ramp so compact table rows meet WCAG AA for normal and large text.

Problem details: 1) When a table row contains an inline input (contenteditable or input[type=text]) followed by an action menu, VoiceOver on macOS/iOS sometimes reads the action menu prior to the editable cell, which confuses users. We believe tabindex ordering and DOM placement for hidden helpers and visually positioned elements are the cause. 2) Inline edit validations use aria-live="assertive" in the current implementation which interrupts sequential reading—this causes the screen reader to jump and lose row context. 3) Color tokens: the compact density variant reuses a muted token that fails AA at 14px in dark theme for the secondary cell label and the 'edited' badge color. Our token scale needs an update and clear mapping for density variants.

Goal: Deliver a remediated component spec and token guidance that: - Ensures deterministic VoiceOver reading order across platforms for complex rows with inline-edit and action menus. - Adds explicit aria attributes and focus management patterns for inline-edit lifecycle (start, commit, cancel) that avoid unexpected live-region interruptions. - Updates color token ramp for compact rows and dark theme to meet WCAG AA at 12–14px. - Provide a VPAT-ready conformance note and test checklist for QA and documentation.
acceptance_criteria: VoiceOver (macOS + iOS) reads dense table rows in logical left-to-right order for all row permutations (cells, inline inputs, action menus).
Keyboard-only users can tab into a row, use arrow keys to navigate between cells, start inline edit with Enter, commit/cancel with Enter/Escape and return focus to a predictable element after action.
Inline edit validation messages are announced without breaking row context (use aria-live polite with smart scoping or aria-describedby anchored to the input).
Compact density and dark theme color token updates meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) for 12–14px body and 3:1 where applicable for UI components, and token mappings are documented.
Design spec updated in Figma and a PR with markup + automated axe tests shipped to github.com/redwood-inference/ui#3456 and merged to canary branch.
tasks: Audit existing table permutations and enumerate cases where VoiceOver misorders readout (Leah to run macOS/iOS VoiceOver scripts).
Propose DOM/focus model: prefer DOM order = visual order; use aria-rowindex/aria-colindex for complex header groupings; avoid tabindex manipulation except for roving tabindex pattern where required.

Define inline-edit ARIA strategy: use role=textbox/native input, aria-label/aria-labelledby, aria-describedby for persistent validation, and aria-live polite in a scoped live region for non-critical updates.
Design token adjustments: produce a 'compact-density token ramp' with delta values for neutral-weak and accent-muted tokens in dark theme. Provide hex + contrast ratios.
Implement quick prototype in Storybook with VoiceOver test harness and add axe/regression tests.
Coordinate with Eng to roll out changes behind a feature flag for console-2025.11, run canary, and monitor telemetry for keyboard/aria regressions.
updates: 2025-10-12 — Kickoff: scoped audit run by Leah; identified 7 distinct permutations where reading order flips when action menu is visually right-aligned and implemented with absolute positioning.

2025-10-18 — Design proposal reviewed with Eng: agreed to prefer DOM order equals visual order; Samir noted several places where CSS transforms were used to reposition action menus — engineering to remove transforms in table rows or provide accessible clones.
2025-10-23 — Token proposal: Maya uploaded compact-density ramp (tokens/neutral-compact-50..900) and initial contrast table. Leah ran contrast checks and flagged three tokens below 4.5:1 at 12px.
2025-10-27 — PR #3456 opened with prototype: implements roving tabindex on row-level and aria-describedby pattern for inline validation. Added Storybook stories for compact/dense table rows.

2025-11-01 — QA pass: accessibility team ran VoiceOver scenarios. Most reading-order regressions resolved; two edge cases remain for iOS VoiceOver and custom action components (tracked as follow-up sub-issue DES-98190).
2025-11-02 — Design decision: use aria-roledescription on grouped rows to provide better context to screen readers; update docs and call out in VPAT notes.
comments: Priya Kapoor (PM) — Please prioritize the compact token ramp changes; enterprise customers have reported legibility issues in dark mode reports. Suggest blocking other DS tasks until token patch is merged.

Samir Patel (Eng) — Implementation note: removing transforms in table rows may affect animations. I'll prototype accessible menu placement that preserves animations via container transforms rather than on the interactive element.

Leah Ortiz (Accessibility) — Live region change validated: switching to aria-live=polite and anchoring messages to inputs preserves sequential readout. Need to document the exact pattern for Web and React Native parity.

Maya Chen (Design) — I've updated the Figma spec with examples for 3 densities and included a diff overlay showing token deltas. Reviewer: @Oliver Hart please confirm focus ring visuals at 2px contrast against background tokens.
Oliver Hart (Design QA) — Confirmed: 2px focus ring meets visibility goals at compact density in light/dark once token neutral-compact-300 is adjusted to #C1C6CB (contrast 4.6:1 at 14px).
